answer.rationale: Write path latency spiked 5x target 90 minutes after a recent release during peak settlement traffic. memory_b1 confirms rollback of a problematic release cleared checkout errors without customer impact previously. memory_b6 shows staged gating can catch regressions early. The timing correlation (release → latency climb) is strong. A rollback is the lowest-risk intervention that directly addresses the most likely root cause. We verify memory_b1 to confirm rollback execution was clean and fast. Routing read replicas (memory_b5) doesn't address write path load; circuit breakers (memory_b4) don't solve latency; failover (memory_b2) is valid but less targeted when the culprit is likely a code change; adding capacity (memory_b3) is slower and doesn't address the probable regression. Rollback preserves availability by stopping the bleeding immediately, protects customer writes by removing the problematic code path, and leaves room to investigate the release offline.
